messages.title: The consumer finished. Why did it run again?
messages.subtitle: A committed reward and a missing acknowledgement can make one logical event arrive twice.
messages.property: One logical event E must not apply its protected reward effect more than once.
messages.takeaway: The repair allows redelivery while preventing this protected effect from repeating.
messages.challenge.title: What prevents the second reward?
messages.challenge.intro: D1(E) added 100 points to User42 and committed. The consumer crashed before the broker durably accepted its ACK. The broker may deliver D2(E).
messages.challenge.question: Which contract keeps D2(E) from adding another 100 points?
messages.option.atomic: Record E and add points in one Rewards Store transaction
messages.option.ackFirst: ACK E before changing the reward balance
messages.option.stableId: Give E a stable ID, but store the marker separately
messages.challenge.feedback: The Rewards Store must atomically bind the processed identity E to the protected +100. ACK-first can lose the effect; a separate marker can be lost after the reward commits.
messages.deepDive.title: A delivery is not the effect
messages.deepDive.section1.title: What the broker knows
messages.deepDive.section1.body: Without a durable ACK, the broker may redeliver E. It cannot infer whether an external Rewards Store transaction committed before the consumer crashed.
messages.deepDive.section2.title: ACK-first moves the gap
messages.deepDive.section2.body: If the broker accepts the ACK first and the consumer crashes before +100 commits, E may never produce its required reward. Reversing two independent actions does not join their durability boundaries.
messages.deepDive.section3.title: The atomic Rewards Store decision
messages.deepDive.section3.body: ApplyEventOnce(E, User42, 100) records E and changes the balance in one transaction. A first delivery makes progress; every later delivery of that same E observes the record and skips the reward mutation.
messages.deepDive.section4.title: Where stable identity is insufficient
messages.deepDive.section4.body: If the +100 commits in the Rewards Store but the processed-E marker lives elsewhere, a crash can leave no marker. D2(E) then repeats +100 despite carrying the same ID.
messages.deepDive.section5.title: Scope and transfer
messages.deepDive.section5.body: A naturally repeat-safe state assignment may need no processed-events table. For inventory reservation, bind ReservationRequested(E) to its decrement at the inventory authority. Neither repair proves one broker delivery or orders distinct events.
messages.visual.title: Effect–Acknowledgement Timeline
messages.visual.ackFirstRisk: ACK first + crash can lose the effect
messages.visual.splitRisk: Separate marker can disappear after +100 commits
messages.rail.evidenceEarly: D1(E) is a delivery of logical event E. The reward has not committed yet.
messages.rail.evidenceGap: +100 committed, but the broker has no durable ACK for E.
messages.rail.evidenceRepeat: D2(E) is the same logical event on a new delivery. The weak consumer committed another +100.
messages.rail.evidenceAckFirst: The broker accepted the ACK, but +100 did not commit before the crash.
messages.rail.evidenceSplit: +100 committed in the Rewards Store, while the separate processed-E marker is absent.
messages.rail.evidenceRepair: The Rewards Store records E together with +100. D2(E) finds E already processed.
messages.rail.contractEarly: The weak consumer commits the reward and ACKs in separate steps.
messages.rail.contractGap: Without a durable ACK, the broker may redeliver E regardless of the reward commit.
messages.rail.contractAckFirst: After accepting ACK, the broker need not redeliver; the reward can be lost.
messages.rail.contractSplit: A processed marker in another durability domain cannot enforce this reward transaction.
messages.rail.contractStrong: ApplyEventOnce makes the E marker and reward mutation one authoritative transaction.
messages.rail.propertyHidden: Will a repeated delivery repeat the protected effect?
messages.rail.property: One logical event E must not apply this protected reward effect more than once.
messages.recap.1: Evidence: +100 committed; a durable ACK did not.
messages.recap.2: Authority: the Rewards Store decides whether E has already changed the balance.
messages.recap.3: Durability: E's processed marker and +100 must survive together.
messages.recap.4: Delivery: D2(E) may arrive without repeating this protected effect.
messages.recap.5: Scope: external effects and publisher identity need their own contracts.
messages.recap.6: Next: distinct events can arrive in the wrong order. Which state supersedes which?
messages.step.review.title: Read the weak consumer
messages.step.review.lead: It changes User42's reward balance, then acknowledges event E. Those actions cross two durability boundaries.
messages.step.first-delivery.title: The first delivery arrives
messages.step.first-delivery.lead: The broker sends D1(E). This is a delivery attempt for logical event E, not a new reward request.
messages.step.reward-commit.title: The reward commits
messages.step.reward-commit.lead: The Rewards Store commits +100 for User42. The protected effect now exists independently of the consumer process.
messages.step.crash-before-ack.title: The consumer crashes
messages.step.crash-before-ack.lead: It crashes before the broker durably accepts its ACK. The committed +100 survives the crash.
messages.step.broker-knowledge.title: What can the broker know?
messages.step.broker-knowledge.lead: The broker has no durable ACK. It cannot read the Rewards Store commit from that missing acknowledgement.
messages.step.redelivery-contract.title: Redelivery is permitted
messages.step.redelivery-contract.lead: Under this broker contract, a missing ACK permits redelivery. The broker has not malfunctioned.
messages.step.second-delivery.title: D2(E) arrives
messages.step.second-delivery.lead: D2 carries the same logical event E. A second delivery need not mean a second business operation.
messages.step.repeated-effect.title: The weak effect repeats
messages.step.repeated-effect.lead: The consumer runs +100 again. User42 has gained 200 points from one E.
messages.step.property.title: Name the violated property
messages.step.property.lead: One logical event E must not apply this protected reward effect more than once. The claim concerns the reward, not the number of deliveries.
messages.step.ack-first.title: Would ACK-first help?
messages.step.ack-first.lead: If ACK commits first and the consumer crashes before the reward, the effect may never happen. Swapping the order trades repetition for loss.
messages.step.event-identity.title: Keep E's identity stable
messages.step.event-identity.lead: Both deliveries must carry the same event identity. A stable ID is necessary for recognizing a repeat, but it does not enforce the reward contract by itself.
messages.step.atomic-apply.title: Make one store decision
messages.step.atomic-apply.lead: ApplyEventOnce records E and adds 100 in one Rewards Store transaction. Either both facts commit or neither does.
messages.step.replay-crash.title: Replay the crash
messages.step.replay-crash.lead: The first ApplyEventOnce commits. The consumer crashes before ACK again; the broker still has reason to redeliver.
messages.step.redelivery-again.title: Redelivery still happens
messages.step.redelivery-again.lead: D2(E) arrives as before. The repair does not require the broker to deliver exactly once.
messages.step.suppress-repeat.title: The second effect is suppressed
messages.step.suppress-repeat.lead: The Rewards Store finds E already recorded. It can complete D2(E) without adding another 100.
messages.step.first-time-control.title: A new event still progresses
messages.step.first-time-control.lead: For a first-time E, the atomic decision records E and adds 100. The guard does not block legitimate rewards.
messages.step.split-durability.title: Split the marker and the gap returns
messages.step.split-durability.lead: If +100 commits but the processed-E marker lives in a separate store, a crash can leave no marker. D2(E) repeats the reward.
messages.step.repeat-safe-control.title: A different effect may already be repeat-safe
messages.step.repeat-safe-control.lead: Setting a shipment to READY twice can be harmless under an explicit repeat-safe contract. Do not prescribe a processed-events table to every consumer.
messages.step.remaining.title: Keep the claim narrow
messages.step.remaining.lead: This repair covers one Rewards Store effect. It does not prove one delivery, one consumer run, or safety for an unrelated external effect.
messages.step.transfer.title: Transfer: reserve inventory
messages.step.transfer.lead: ReservationRequested(E) decrements available inventory by one. Where must E's processed identity be bound so D2(E) cannot decrement again?
messages.step.recap.title: Six questions, one boundary
messages.step.recap.lead: Use the evidence, authority, durability, and delivery questions to explain the repaired trace, then carry the remaining ordering question forward.
